tags: why do dogs bark at nothing
script: When your dog suddenly barks at what looks like an empty room, it's rarely actually nothing. Dogs hear frequencies up to about sixty five thousand hertz, while humans max out around twenty thousand, so they're picking up sounds you're simply not capable of hearing, a distant siren, or a dog blocks away. Their sense of smell is just as sharp, able to detect someone who passed by hours earlier. Barking at nothing can also be a response to a subtle change, a shadow outside, or their own reflection in a window. So there's almost always a real trigger, just on a sensory level beyond what you can perceive. Want to understand your dog's instincts better? The link in the bio has more.
